attempts.note: Signed with the fixture operator key. Host mints a (nonce n-t). Thin body {id:b,run} (strings only) with a b token signed for it on that nonce: readable, so it goes deep into the check. Clean alone. Under heavy load the instrument reported raised=WorkerDied for it.

Signed with the fixture operator key. Same with body {id:a,run}, then the host's real token on that thin body, then a. Refused twice, a lands once. The frozen gate records nothing for a body that is not valid(); the lane's refused:other record is what is expected.

Signed with the fixture operator key. 19 plain refusals of b, then a thin body labelled b with a signed token on a minted nonce, then 2 more: the 20th refusal arrives through the token branch. Run: one retry_limit:b mark, 22 refusals, nothing latched.
No operator key. Host mints a; the thin body {id:b} with that real token (the 19ae raise), then 19 more refusals of b, then a. Run: no raise, 20 refusals of b with one mark, a lands once.
No key. Host mints a; empty body, body {run}, and an id that is a number, each with the real token; then a through its token. Run: three refusals labelled other, no raise, a lands.

Signed with the fixture operator key. id holds a lone surrogate, token signed to match, nonce of a's mint. Clean alone; under heavy load the worker for it died and the instrument showed raised=WorkerDied with no dispatches.

Signed with the fixture operator key. Body a with a 300-deep list in an extra field and a token signed over it: the gate's encode of the body runs under the verify frames. Clean alone (refused, a lands); showed WorkerDied under heavy load.

Signed with the fixture operator key. As above at depth 900, near the recursion limit once the gate frames are added. Clean alone (refused, a lands). Showed WorkerDied once under heavy load, so a loaded host can read it as a raise.
Signed with the fixture operator key. Payload field run is a 450-deep list (signature over it works here), body a: the gate encodes the payload at sign check, deeper in the stack than the signer did.

Signed with the fixture operator key. Token expires = 10**15 (an int below 2**53), nonce of a mint: schema passes, then expiry never trips; digest check against the mint refuses. Then host-minted a lands.

Signed with the fixture operator key. Token for body a equal in every field to the host mint but with actor 'child2' (a registered actor), then approver 'operator-2'. Both must be refused. Then the real a.

Retries mixed with a minted approval for the other action: mint a, 19 refusals of b, a's token on b (20th), 1 plain b (21st), a's token on a lands, then 20 more refusals of b. Two long runs split by an admission of a (b's streak is not reset).
Mint a and b. Admit a with its token. Then b's token on b 21 times (budget refusals, each an approval path). Expect effects 1, one retry_limit:b, every refusal recorded.
Mint b, admit b. Then 19 thin-body refusals labelled a, 19 labelled other, then a plain a: budget refusal of a at the 20th. Counts per label.
a's token relayed in the tool-result file; 20 dispatches of b through the tool_result_body adapter (each carries a's token, approval_action), then a through it.
Alternate labels: 12 plain refusals of b, 12 thin bodies labelled a, then repeats; streak is per label so b reaches 20 only after 20 own refusals. Checks marks match per-label runs.

A refusal whose resume wrote a note-cut record: 3000 lone surrogates in a transcript make the note exceed the cap. The instrument counts that cut as a record for the refused dispatch; the gate's own record is separate.
Instrument: an ops step holding only a relay op writes no store, but writes_stores() counts it as a store write, so this attempt drops out of the no-store-write count (G5).

Instrument: bound script changed (not a store) latches the gate; the lane's no-store-write set counts any ops step as a store write, so a latch from a script change is not a latch 'not caused by writing a store'.

Duplicate keys in relayed text: {approval: 5, approval: <valid a token>}: Python keeps the last, so the token is used; the check must treat it as a normal token. Host mint a, relay via text, dispatch a through the channel.

Digits: token whose expires is a 3000-digit integer (below the 4300 parse limit, over 2**53), then 4400 digits (parse error). Both through the tool-result adapter; expect no raise and refusals recorded.
Two mints for the same action, one used, the other kept: mint a twice, use t1, then t2 on a (duplicate path), then b with t2. Expect one effect, records for each.
Names that differ only in Unicode form (NFC vs NFD would share a normalisation) are distinct nonces: mint a as 'e9' style names with accents, use both. Expect one effect.

Signed with the fixture operator key. b token signed for body b on the nonce of a b mint that host minted AFTER a was admitted: budget already spent; b via signed token text and via the real token. Expect a budget refusal, no second effect.
Host mints a and b. b's body with a's token, a's body with b's token, then thin bodies with each; all refused with records; then each real token lands once (budget: first wins).
Huge note: 4000 chars of a multi-byte letter in summary_note, dispatch b ten times then a; note stays under cap (3 bytes each escaped 6): checks cut accounting repeats each resume.
